slides.heading: Combining Comparisons
slides.body: Combining Comparisons is part of Boolean Logic and Comparisons. This short lesson gives you a practical Python idea you can understand, try, and reuse in simple programs.

slides.heading: Core Idea: Combining Comparisons
slides.body: Multiple comparisons can be combined to check ranges or complex rules. Parentheses can make the logic easier to read.

slides.heading: Real-World Analogy
slides.body: Combining comparisons is like checking a scholarship requirement: grade, documents, and deadline must all be considered.

slides.heading: Key Rule
slides.body: Boolean expressions must produce True or False. Use comparisons and logical operators carefully.

slides.heading: Try It Yourself!
slides.prompt: Check whether age is between 13 and 19 inclusive.

coding_challenge.prompt_text: Print whether points is greater than 0 and less than 10.
coding_challenge.hint_text: Use the idea from the lesson. Keep the code short, readable, and correctly indented.
